## Dīgha Nikāya
## Pāthikavagga Pāḷi
## Homage to the Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.

## 1. Pāthika Sutta
## The Story of Sunakkhatta

Thus have I heard: At one time the Blessed One was staying among the Mallans, at a town of the Mallans named Anupiya. Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, and taking his bowl and robe, entered Anupiya for alms. Then the thought occurred to the Blessed One: "It is still too early to wander for alms in Anupiya. What if I were to approach the park of the wanderer Bhaggavagotta, where the wanderer Bhaggavagotta is?"

Then the Blessed One approached the park of the wanderer Bhaggavagotta, where the wanderer Bhaggavagotta was. Then the wanderer Bhaggavagotta said to the Blessed One: "Come, Blessed One! Welcome, Blessed One! It has been a long time since the Blessed One made this journey to come here. Please sit down, Blessed One; this seat is prepared." The Blessed One sat on the prepared seat. The wanderer Bhaggavagotta also took a low seat and sat to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Bhaggavagotta said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, in former times..."
2: Indeed, that wanderer Bhaggavagotta took a low seat and sat in a certain place. Sitting in that place, the wanderer Bhaggavagotta addressed the Blessed One thus: "Venerable sir, some days ago, and even earlier, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince approached me. Having approached, he said to me: 'Bhaggava, I have now renounced the Blessed One. I no longer live dedicated to the Blessed One as my teacher.' Venerable sir, is that statement true, just as Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince said?" "Bhaggava, that statement is indeed true, just as Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince said," the Blessed One replied. Bhaggava, some days ago, and even earlier, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince approached me. Having approached, he paid homage to me and sat to one side. Sitting to one side, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince said to me: "Venerable sir, I now renounce the Blessed One. I will no longer live dedicated to the Blessed One, venerable sir." When he had said this, Bhaggava, I said to Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince: "Sunakkhatta, did I ever say to you, 'Sunakkhatta, come, live dedicated to me'?" "No, venerable sir," he replied. "Or did you ever say to me, 'Venerable sir, I will live dedicated to the Blessed One'?" "No, venerable sir," he replied. "So, Sunakkhatta, since I did not say to you, 'Sunakkhatta, come, live dedicated to me,' and you did not say to me, 'Venerable sir, I will live dedicated to the Blessed One,' this being so, you foolish man, who are you that you renounce whom? See, foolish man, how far you have gone wrong in this." "Venerable sir, the Blessed One does not perform for me any superhuman feat of psychic power," Sunakkhatta replied. "Sunakkhatta, did I ever say to you, 'Sunakkhatta, come, live dedicated to me, and I will perform for you a superhuman feat of psychic power'?" "No, venerable sir," he replied. "Or did you ever say to me, 'Venerable sir, I will live dedicated to the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will perform for me a superhuman feat of psychic power'?" "No, venerable sir," he replied. "So, Sunakkhatta, since I did not say to you, 'Sunakkhatta, come, live dedicated to me, and I will perform for you a superhuman feat of psychic power,' and you did not say to me, 'Venerable sir, I will live dedicated to the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will perform for me a superhuman feat of psychic power,' this being so, you foolish man, who are you that you renounce whom? Sunakkhatta, what do you think? Whether a superhuman feat of psychic power is performed or not..."
3:
“Whether a miracle of superhuman power is performed or not, the Dhamma has been taught by me for the purpose of the complete destruction of suffering—Nibbāna—for the one who practices accordingly. Does that Dhamma not lead the one who practices it to the complete destruction of suffering?” “Venerable Sir, whether a miracle of superhuman power is performed or not, the Dhamma has been taught by the Blessed One for that purpose; and it does lead the one who practices it to the complete destruction of suffering.” “Sunakkhatta, if the Dhamma I taught leads the one who practices it to the complete destruction of suffering regardless of whether a miracle of superhuman power is performed or not, then what purpose would the performance of a miracle of superhuman power serve? See, foolish man, how far you have gone astray.”

“Venerable Sir, the Blessed One does not declare to me the beginning of the world (Aggañña).” “Sunakkhatta, did I ever say to you, ‘Come, Sunakkhatta, live under my guidance, and I will declare to you the beginning of the world’?” “No, Venerable Sir.” “Or did you say to me, ‘Venerable Sir, I will live under the Blessed One’s guidance, and the Blessed One will declare to me the beginning of the world’?” “No, Venerable Sir.” “Sunakkhatta, since I did not say this to you, and you did not say this to me, you foolish man, being who you are, whom are you rejecting? Sunakkhatta, what do you think? Whether the beginning of the world is declared or not, does the Dhamma I taught lead the one who practices it to the complete destruction of suffering?” “Venerable Sir, whether the beginning of the world is declared or not, the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One leads the one who practices it to the complete destruction of suffering.” “Sunakkhatta, if the Dhamma I taught leads to the complete destruction of suffering regardless of whether the beginning of the world is declared or not, then what purpose would declaring the beginning of the world serve? See, foolish man, how far you have gone astray.”

“Sunakkhatta, you have spoken my praises in many ways in the city of Vesālī in the Vajji country: ‘That Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, accomplished in true knowledge and conduct...’ ”
